title: Product Release Development Process for Validated Systems
summary: Defines the end-to-end development process from user story creation through release delivery within a QMS-governed SDLC. Covers cross-functional roles, weekly build cadence, stabilization, change management, and all output deliverables required for GxP compliance.

findings.purpose_and_scope: Spans from creating user stories describing the release backlog to delivering the release and all appropriate material. Operates within the QMS framework and is aligned to ISO 9001:2015 section 8.3. GxP-aligned for regulated life sciences environments.
findings.cross_functional_roles: Over 15 defined roles with detailed responsibilities: General Manager (go/no-go authority), Product Management (backlog ownership, user stories, UAT), Product Engineering (development, code quality), Product Testing (test execution, quality gates), Product Documentation, Go-To-Market, Sales Engineering, Technical Sales Engineering, Product Marketing, Product DevOps, UI/UX, Product Support, Product Operations, QMS Core Team, Delivery, Partnership, and PMO.
findings.development_flow: Release content is defined and user stories are created and prioritized by Product Management. A kickoff meeting aligns all teams. Teams plan and allocate work. Engineering develops features with weekly build cadence. Stabilization phase follows development. All materials are delivered and General Manager issues go/no-go decision. Final handoff to Product Operations and Delivery teams.
findings.change_management: Change requests during development may impact scope or timeline. Bug triage determines whether defects are fixed as part of the current release (patch) or postponed to a future release. Formal change request process tracks scope modifications.
findings.lifecycle_flowcharts: Four sub-views of the full lifecycle flowchart, plus dedicated flowcharts for development detail and stabilization phases. A separate launch flowchart covers go-to-market activities.
findings.output_deliverables: Fifteen required deliverables including: Go/No-Go Decision, Release Notes, Functional Documentation, Technical Documentation, Installation Guide, Test Results, Webinar recordings, Marketing Collaterals, Training Materials, Demo Scenarios, Validation documentation, Escrow Agreement, and Disaster Recovery Plan.
findings.kpi: Number of developed user stories versus number of planned user stories for the release.

source: SOP-0014[3] Product Release Development, ISO 9001:2015 section 8.3, effective Apr 2019
